translation: Target defines the proposition that for all types X and Y, for every finite-node machine N (consisting of a finite type of nodes, a state type for each node, an initial global state assigning an initial value to each node, a per-node update function mapping the current global state and an input in X to that node's next value, and an output function mapping a global state to Y), and for every natural number T (including T = 0), with no additional hypotheses on X, Y, N, or T, the layered machine N' obtained from N and T satisfies three conditions simultaneously. Here N' has node set {0, ..., T - 1} × (nodes of N), where node (t, n) has the same state type and initial value as node n of N; on input x from global state σ, node (t, n) updates using N's update rule for n applied to input x and either N's fixed initial global state (when t = 0) or the slice of σ at layer t - 1 (when t > 0); and the output function of N' applies N's output function to N's initial global state when T = 0, or to the slice of σ at layer T - 1 when T > 0. The three conditions asserted of N' are: (1) N' has no directed cycles of length 1 or more in its dependency relation, where there is a directed edge from node a to node b whenever there exist two global states of N' agreeing on all nodes other than a and an input x in X for which b's update function produces different values on the two states (so neither self-loops nor longer cycles occur); (2) N' and N produce the exact same output in Y on every finite sequence of inputs from X—with no restriction on the length of the sequence (in particular, not restricted to sequences of length at most T)—where the output on a sequence is obtained by starting from the initial global state, synchronously updating all nodes left-to-right for each input in the sequence, and then applying the output function; and (3) the number of nodes of N' equals T times the number of nodes of N.

divergences.description: Target asserts S1.D6 (N.d14 T) N—that the T-step unrolled system has the same input-output behavior as N on all finite input sequences of arbitrary length—rather than S1.D5 T (N.d14 T) N (equivalence on sequences of length at most T). This contradicts both the author's claim ('over T steps') and the unrolling-through-time justification in Herzog et al. (where T copies simulate T timesteps), and it makes Target mathematically false: for any T, the unrolling N.d14 T only tracks at most the last T inputs (and is constant when T = 0), so on a recurrent latch such as d15 it disagrees with N on an input sequence of length T + 1 (e.g., true followed by T copies of false).

Target quantifies over all systems N : S1 X Y (including non-recurrent ones and the degenerate horizon T = 0), whereas P2 and the source passages state the claim for recurrent networks/systems and positive durations; this is a harmless strengthening (and the quantification over all systems is declared by the author).

The formal model S1 idealizes the general networks/systems of Doerig et al. and Herzog et al. as finite-unit, deterministic, discrete-time, synchronous machines mapping finite input lists to a single output, and defines 'feedforward' (D9) via acyclicity of functional state-sensitivity rather than physical/structural wiring.

judgement.summary: Target is divergent because it asserts unbounded-length input-output equivalence (S1.D6) rather than T-step bounded equivalence (S1.D5 T) for the T-layer unrolling N.d14 T, contradicting the 'over T steps' unrolling claim and rendering the formalized proposition false.
